title: Stability of Bioactive Compounds and Antioxidant Capacity in Fresh and Commercial Mixed-Plant Beverages
content: Fruit and vegetable beverages are rich sources of bioactive compounds with potent antioxidant capacity, playing a key role in mitigating oxidative stress and chronic inflammation. Epidemiological evidence suggests that these dietary bioactive compounds may prevent oxidative damage, reducing disease risk and promoting overall health benefits. The aim of this study was to determine the total phenolic content (TPC) and antioxidant activity (AA) of commercial fruit and vegetables beverage and its manufactured equivalent beverage over time (t0-0min; t1-24h and t2-72h). Folin-Ciocalteu and Ferric Reducing Antioxidant Potential (FRAP) assay were used for TPC and AA characterization, respectively. Commercial beverage revealed significantly higher TPC and AA values (p < 0.001) (t0- 308.47; t1- 415.97 and t2- 398.29 gallic acid mg/L and t0- 2.10; t1- 2.24 and t2- 2.38 trolox equivalent mmol /L) than its manufactured equivalent beverage. Commercial and manufactured beverages revealed differences for the 3 moments studied. A significant positive correlation between total phenolic content and antioxidant properties highlights the contribution of these bioactive compounds in neutralizing oxidative stress. Although both commercial and manufactured beverages maintained stability when stored at 4 °C for up to 72 h, the commercial beverage showed higher overall antioxidant capacity, supporting its potential role in enhancing dietary antioxidant intake to combat inflammation and oxidative stress.
